take_homes: Hand the synthesizer a framework (diagnosis, guiding policy, actions) so it commits to one answer instead of averaging three views.
Split by access, dialect or stance only; otherwise one good prompt wins.
The handoffs are where it breaks (a curator silently dropping one of two conflicting numbers), and the audit doesn't tell you if the final briefing is true.

monday.move: Take one recurring workflow from the sales team's stack, set up a retriever for each of its two sources, and add a synthesizer with the kernel prompt. I'll also have one agent list the numbers the curator dropped.
monday.who: Me, plus one engineer to review the seams
monday.stop_condition: If the curator can't show me which conflicting numbers it dropped, I don't roll it out to sales.
monday.blocker: Nobody in sales has asked for it yet, and I haven't decided who maintains it.

misconception.why: The curator keeping one of two numbers, and the 'nothing here checks if the briefing is true' beat, made me see that a setup can work and still produce a wrong answer. I still think I'd catch it by eye, so checking isn't only for beginners, but I'd now check the seams.

one_line: Good rules for when to split and the framework trick is worth stealing, but it's paced for people who haven't run agents, and the crux exercise wasn't something I'd have found alone.
